challenges.name: menu-cache-singleflight
challenges.title: Cache the menus without a stampede
challenges.description: The gateway cached each restaurant's menu for 60 s. When the entry for a popular restaurant expired at lunch, hundreds of requests missed at once and all called the menu service, which fell over; failed calls were cached too, so customers saw an empty menu for a minute. The editor holds `menucache.go` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that `Get`: returns an entry younger than `ttlMs` without calling the menu service; makes concurrent misses for the same key share one call and all receive its result; never caches a failed call; and serves the expired entry when a refresh fails (stale-if-error). Run sends bursts of concurrent requests and counts the calls the menu service gets.
hints: Follow two goroutines that miss at the same moment: which one calls the menu service, where does the other wait, and what must happen to the shared call once it is finished so the next expiry starts a new one?

Look at the TTL check in the fresh-hit block, the `inflight` map (join an existing call, wait on `done`), what is written to `entries` on success and on failure, and the order of storing the result, removing the call and closing `done`.

A token cache with the same shape: `if t, ok := c.tokens[user]; ok && c.now() < t.expires { return t.value, nil }`, `if f, ok := c.pending[user]; ok { c.mu.Unlock(); <-f.ready; return f.token, f.err }`, and after the login call `if err == nil { c.tokens[user] = token{...} }; f.token, f.err = tok, err; delete(c.pending, user); close(f.ready)`.

tests.name: 200 requests at the lunch rush share one call to the menu service
Within the TTL every request is served from the cache
After the TTL, 200 requests refresh the menu with one call
A failed call is not cached: the next request tries again
When the menu service is down after the TTL, the last menu is still served
